_comment: Inputs to scripts/check_alerts.py, which the weekly workflow runs after collection. Crossing a threshold opens a GitHub issue. It does not mean something is wrong; it means the week is worth looking at, which is the only thing an automated check can honestly claim.
_lookback_note: The comparison is against the most recent observation at least 7 days older than the latest one, searching back this far to find it. Index series skip holidays, so a fixed 7-day offset frequently lands on a day with no observation.
_staleness_note: If the newest observation in a series is older than this, the source has probably stopped updating or the collector has silently stopped working. That is worth an issue on its own.

fred_move._comment: Absolute week-over-week move that triggers an issue. Spread series in basis points, yields in percentage points. Set wide enough that ordinary weeks stay quiet: the point of an alert that fires every week is nothing.

price_gap_move_pct._comment: Relative change in the open versus closed weights price advantage at the mid-tier capability floor, on the fp8 base case, as a percentage of last week's ratio. This is the number the elasticity pillar exists to track, so a large move in it is the most important thing the weekly run can surface.

expected_rows._comment: Minimum rows a collector should add on a run that is supposed to collect. Zero rows from a collector that ran without error is the failure mode that would otherwise go unnoticed for weeks. An entry may be a bare number, in which case the file checked is data/scorecard/<key>.csv, or an object with an explicit path and min, for collectors that write outside the scorecard directory.
expected_rows._credit_note: `credit` was here at 20 and fired a false positive on the first automated run, 2026-11-02. FRED had published nothing new since 2026-10-29, so appending zero rows was correct behaviour rather than a failure. A publisher with a lag cannot be monitored by counting rows per run; it is monitored by staleness, which is what `staleness_days` above already does and which correctly stayed quiet. Removed rather than retuned, because any row count would be wrong in some week.
expected_rows._filings_note: The filings extractor is deliberately absent for the same reason: it adds nothing in most weeks by design, because filings are quarterly.
expected_rows._elasticity_note: The OpenRouter collector now writes raw per-model prices to data/elasticity_prices.csv rather than to the pillar file, so the row-count check follows the raw file. The pillar file data/scorecard/elasticity.csv gains only three aggregate rows a run, far below any useful floor, and is covered by the staleness check instead. See docs/decisions.md, 2026-11-03.
